subject: Clarify: how reranker/classifier scoring is billed + pilot terms
messages:
From: Sara Park <sara@searchly.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Briggs <tbrigg@searchly.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reranker pricing: per-score vs per-call?

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo last week — Tom and I walked through the live rerank prototype and we loved the latency. Before we take the technical POC, procurement has asked for a clear rate card for the reranker/classifier endpoints. Two specific questions that keep coming up on our side:

- Do you bill rerank/classifier evaluation by tokens (like generation) or by "scoring units" (e.g., candidates * calls)?
- If scoring units, what counts as a unit (each candidate scored, each returned top-k, or per-request)?

For context, our expected baseline: 10M user queries/month, average candidate set 50 items, 95th percentile latency objective ~120ms. We anticipate a 3-month pilot (up to 3M queries/month) before moving to a committed annual contract.

Can you share a sample enterprise rate card and a pilot discount / cap you typically offer for a POC? Also: any recommendations to reduce unit cost (batch endpoints, candidate-side pruning, better candidate recall strategies)?

Appreciate quick clarity — procurement wants a pricing line item they can feed into the SOW.

Best,
Sara
Head of Search, Searchly

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Park <sara@searchly.com>
Cc: Tom Briggs <tbrigg@searchly.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reranker pricing: per-score vs per-call?

Sara — thanks for the clear context and the sample. Short answers up front: we bill reranker/classifier evaluation as scoring units (not token-based), and a unit = one candidate scored by the model. In other words: scoring_units = calls * number_of_candidates_evaluated.

Details and options:
- Per-score unit pricing: cheapest to reason about for rerank workloads where candidate set size varies.
- Per-request pricing: offered as a convenience for very small candidate sets (<5), but it usually ends up more expensive at scale.
- Token-billing applies to text generation endpoints; rerank/classifier is unit-based because the bulk cost is model forward passes over candidates.

To reduce cost: batch evaluation (we can accept arrays of candidate sets and amortize KV cache), candidate-side pre-filtering, and quantized model variants. Aditya — included you on cc to confirm the unit math below and whether we can auto-detect/normalize candidate counts for the pilot.

I've attached our Q3 sample rate card and a pilot SOW template. Proposal for initial pilot: 3-month pilot, up to 3M queries/month, billed at $0.35 per 1k scoring units with a 40% pilot discount capped at $20k total spend. If we detect you need a per-request option for any low-cardinality endpoints we can add that as a line item.

Next steps: if that works, Marcus will approve the specific discount and we can run a quick SOW.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reranker pricing: per-score vs per-call? (unit math + batching)

Quick technical confirmation and pricing math from infra side:

- Definition: scoring_unit = 1 forward pass for 1 candidate (includes tokenization + forward). If you score 50 candidates for a query, that is 50 scoring units.
- Billing granularity: we bill per 1,000 scoring units (we call them KU). Example: 10M queries/month * 50 candidates = 500M scoring units -> 500,000 KU. At $0.35 per KU -> $175k/mo (list).
- Batching benefit: with continuous batching and KV-cache warm paths, effective cost can drop ~20-30% on typical workloads because you amortize overhead and reduce per-forward latency. For pilots, we can enable an experimental batch pricing where we invoice based on effective KU measured post-batching (we log raw and effective KU to the invoice).
- Savings levers: reduce candidate set size (re-rank top N), use a cheaper quantized rerank model for filtering, or run a lightweight classifier first to prune candidates.

If Searchly wants a per-request flat SKU for a small set of endpoints, we can do that but recommend it only for <5 candidates on average.

— Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reranker pricing: per-score vs per-call? (pilot approval)

Thanks team — reviewed. Grace: authorized to offer the following pilot terms to Searchly:

- Pilot length: 3 months (starts on sign).
- Pilot cap: $20k total spend (as Grace proposed).
- Pilot unit price: $0.35 per KU (1 KU = 1k scoring units), applied after 40% pilot discount. Example: list price 0.35/KU -> pilot price 0.21/KU.
- Experimental batch pricing: track effective KU; if effective KU reduction >10%, apply an additional 10% rebate (applied at pilot close).

Grace — please route the SOW to Legal and cc me on the HubSpot deal. Sara/Tom — once you sign the SOW we will provision pilot capacity in your org and provide a short onboarding runbook.

Marcus Lin
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
